title: Senior's toolkit: proxies, CDNs and tunnels
summary: Go through or around a corporate proxy, read what a CDN or load balancer did to a request, and reach private services with SSH and WireGuard.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: proxies, CDNs and tunnels
steps.body: Between a client and your app sit proxies, CDNs, load balancers and tunnels. These commands show what each one does to a request, and get you to private services safely.

toolkit.what: The environment variables curl, git, pip, npm, .NET and most CLIs read to use a corporate proxy. `NO_PROXY` keeps internal names off it.
flags: proxy for https URLs (lowercase `https_proxy` is the safest spelling across tools)
comma list of hosts and domain suffixes to reach directly
a proxy for one curl call
ignore the proxy for this call
toolkit.when: builds work at home but not in the office, or the other way round

toolkit.what: Response headers only, from a real GET. CDN and load-balancer headers say whether the cache hit, how old the copy is and which edge answered.
flags: seconds the cached copy has been held
HIT or MISS (names vary by CDN)

toolkit.what: Local port forward: `localhost:5432` on your laptop now reaches the private database through the bastion. Nothing is exposed to the internet.
flags: forward a local port to a target, as seen from the SSH server
no remote shell, just the tunnel
go to the background after login
the reverse: expose a local port on the remote side

toolkit.what: Jumps through a bastion to a private host in one command, with end-to-end SSH. Put it in `~/.ssh/config` as `ProxyJump` and forget it.
flags: the `~/.ssh/config` form, also used by scp, rsync and VS Code Remote-SSH

toolkit.what: A SOCKS proxy through the bastion. Point a browser or `curl --socks5-hostname` at it to reach internal web UIs.
flags: resolve names on the far side too

toolkit.what: WireGuard status: each peer, its endpoint, allowed IPs and the time of the latest handshake. No recent handshake means the tunnel is not up.
flags: should be under about 2 minutes on an active tunnel
which destinations are routed into this peer
bring a configured tunnel up or down

toolkit.what: Checks whether your app trusts a client-supplied forwarding header. If logs or rate limits now show 1.2.3.4, anyone can spoof their address.
flags: the standard form of the same idea
the app should only accept these headers from known proxy addresses

steps.prompt: Match each command to what it gives you.
pairs: a local port that reaches the private database
a shell on a private host through a jump box
a SOCKS proxy into the private network
the WireGuard peers and their latest handshakes
internal names bypass the corporate proxy

steps.prompt: In the office, `dotnet restore` works but calls from your app to `https://orders.corp.internal` fail with `403 Forbidden` from a server named `squid`. At home both work. What is wrong?
options: The proxy is applied to internal names too; add `.corp.internal` to `NO_PROXY` (and `no_proxy`)
The orders service blocks the office
The certificate on orders has expired
steps.explain: The 403 comes from the proxy, not the service: the request went to squid, which will not fetch internal addresses. `NO_PROXY` sends those names directly.

steps.prompt: You deployed a fixed `app.js`, but users still get the old one. `curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://www.example.com/app.js` shows `cf-cache-status: HIT` and `age: 41230`. What is the real fix?
options: Serve assets under content-hashed file names (`app.3f9c1e.js`) so each deploy gets a new URL; purge the CDN for now
Tell users to clear their cache
steps.explain: The edge holds an 11-hour-old copy that it may keep until `max-age` runs out. Hashed names make long caching safe, because a new build never reuses a URL.

steps.prompt: Reach the private Postgres at `db.internal:5432` through the bastion, on local port 15432, without opening a shell.
steps.explain: `-L` forwards a local port to a target as seen from the bastion, and `-N` skips the remote shell. `-R` would forward the other way.

steps.prompt: Local forward, jump host or SOCKS proxy?
items: Run a database GUI on your laptop against a private DB
Get a shell on a private VM
`scp` a file to a private host
Point one local port at an internal Redis
Let `curl` resolve internal names from the far side

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Put your bastions in `~/.ssh/config` with `ProxyJump`, and use `ssh -L` instead of opening database ports to the internet. When a request behaves differently on different networks, check the proxy variables and the CDN headers before you debug the app.
